speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. When did you deliver your baby, and have you noticed any foul-smelling discharge or persistent uterine tenderness?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any pain or burning sensation when urinating, and have you noticed any fever or chills since delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you had any vaginal bleeding or lochia, and does it have a foul odor? I need to rule out endometritis given your fever and uterine tenderness.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Uncomplicated pregnancy leading up to a vaginal delivery. No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: Does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. Lives with her partner.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. To further evaluate your symptoms, I need to check your current vital signs and inflammatory markers. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count REQUEST TEST: C-Reactive_Protein

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC Pending, Hemoglobin Pending, Platelets Pending. C-Reactive_Protein: Not in data.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see the blood work is pending. Do you have any lower back pain or flank pain, which might suggest a kidney infection?

speaker: Patient
text: Complains of minor difficulty in breathing but denies any urinary pain, headache, vomiting, or diarrhea.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the prolonged labor, large baby, and uterine tenderness with fever, endometritis is highly likely, but I must rule out pulmonary embolism due to your breathing difficulty. I need to see your vital signs and oxygen saturation immediately. REQUEST TEST: Vital_Signs REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital_Signs: Temperature 102°F (38.9°C), Blood_Pressure 118/78 mmHg, Heart_Rate 111/min, Respiratory_Rate 17/min, Oxygen_Saturation 98% on room air. Chest_X-Ray: Not in data.

speaker: Doctor
text: You have a high fever, tachycardia, and uterine tenderness, which strongly points to postpartum endometritis rather than a pulmonary issue given your normal oxygen saturation. I am requesting a pelvic ultrasound to confirm the diagnosis and rule out any retained products of conception. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Despite the lack of imaging confirmation, your clinical presentation of postpartum fever, tachycardia, and uterine tenderness following a prolonged labor with a large baby is classic for endometritis. I am proceeding with treatment for this diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Endometritis
